excerpt: Local AI Tool Engine L.A.T.E. takes a local model (or an API model) and turns it into an agent. You give it a goal, and it works through it: it picks a tool, runs it, reads what came back, and keeps going until the job is done. Search the web, read pages and files, do exact maths, save files, remember things between chats. I built it because models on their own are bad at the boring parts. They get maths wrong, forget everything when the chat ends, and make things up instead of looking them up. Small models are worse: they skip steps, count letters in their head and lose track halfway through a job. So here the tools do the exact work, plain code handles the order of the steps, and the model mostly writes the answer. It runs with Ollama, LM Studio, or an API key (Groq, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini, anything OpenAI-compatible). No LangChain, no paid API needed, two dependencies. - Exact answers. Maths, dates, unit conversion, counting, random numbers and weather come from real tools, not from the model's memory. - Multi-step jobs. "Create a file, read it back, count the characters, save the count, read that file too" runs as exact steps, in order, and the answer lists what really happened. Works even when the model is tiny. - Research with sources. It searches, opens the best pages, answers from what it read, and links them. - Your files. Read a file, search a folder, copy, merge, sort the lines, change case, append text. - Memory. Tell it something once, it remembers in later chats. forget really removes it. - Saving files. Only after you say yes, and only into an ai-output folder. - Terminal or browser. A terminal chat, or a small web page on your own computer. - Rules first, model last. The plan for a job is made by plain code (the same words give the same plan every time). The model only writes text. A job is never answered with "here's how you could do it": it runs, or it says plainly that it couldn't. - It says what really happened. The answer lists the steps…
